midseason-7.label: Mid-Season Report Card

blurbs.austin-cyborg-squad: This is pretty comfortably one of the worst teams this league has ever seen, probably just behind Austin’s team last season and Austin’s team in 2022 that also finished last (are you sensing the pattern?). Only one win against the median, no wins at all since week 2, just 0.4 points above the league’s lowest scorer, and Evans’ injury last night cemented Austin’s place in the basement right below Ty. Comparing Austin’s management skills to Billy Napier might be an insult to Billy at this point. At least Lamar is back, right?
blurbs.tyler-team-strong-2025: That Mike Evans injury really had Ty breathing a sigh of relief, because things would have been bleak otherwise. Tenth in total points, the first three picks have been way underperforming, the QB might get benched in real life, and to top it all off, Ty only has one home run in softball. With Saquon not being able to run, everyone else sucking, and all of the bad injuries, there’s very little to look forward to for the rest of the season. The win over Austin last night might legitimately be impactful, in that it could have saved Ty from the wings. Maybe not though.
blurbs.matt-the-team-formerly-known-as-jeanty-i: Maybe I was too kind in ranking this team as high as I have been; I mean, they’ve only seen one win vs. median all season, which is the same as basement-dweller Austin. Without finding Javonte late, this team would be an eternal dumpster fire. Early QB doesn’t work when the guy can’t play, Ladd and Nico aren’t consistent, Jeanty can’t score because his offense blows. What is there really to look forward to, Burrow coming back in 2 months? In a way, this team name is apt: Matt’s team blew their load on their one median win, and now it’s just a giant mess that needs cleaning up.
blurbs.rocco-team-of-bums-v8: These last two weeks have really turned things around for Rocco’s team. I mean, after week 5, we were looking at a team with no hope at all, that was far and away the worst team in the league, way in last in points scored. And now… well we’re still last in points, but the vibes are way better! A wise man once said, happiness is expectations minus reality. Sure, the starting lineup is kind of awful, and sure, there’s not a lot to look forward to each week, and sure, projections for this team are still awful. But we’ve known for weeks that this team can’t possibly be a playoff team, so now the expectations are so low that every win feels like a celebration. No wings for now! *knocks on wood*
blurbs.richard-the-pollard-express: Last week was a massive derailment for the Pollard Express, and really a perfect embodiment of their season so far; it looks like things are finally getting on track, getting some consistency, and then boom, debris on the tracks, passage to the North Pole is delayed. I gotta hold my hand up and take the L on Mahomes, I thought he’d be bad yet again but he’s been unreal for fantasy this year, and arguably the one saving grace for Richard’s team. It does kinda suck to take all of those running backs and have so few of them be good. The median record does provide some hope, but having multiple Dolphins in 2025 kinda quashes the hope as soon as you start to have it. Maybe Mahomes can carry this patchwork team to victory like he has the Chiefs the past few seasons.
blurbs.steven-i-am-a-stupid-idiot: It’s possible this ranking and Steven’s total points are heavily inflated by a stellar week 2, but I think things are starting to look up a bit for Steven. After this week, his best players will have served their byes, and the trade for Henry probably made his team stronger in the long run. The team seems pretty feast-or-famine each week, scoring either >110 or <90, but that gives me hope that the 110 is possible more consistently as the season goes on. Or not, and just like Steven, this team could roll their ankle right after this and immediately find themselves done with the year. Maybe I should believe less in a team with Daniel Jones as its QB.
blurbs.liam-rasheez-nuts: Liam dared me to rank him 8th again, but I couldn’t bring myself to do it. Now that his WRs are out of jail, things are really starting to look up for the Nuts; we were getting intense blue balls imagining what this team could be, and now we’re seeing them at their full potential, and it might just bring us to completion. The RB depth is bad, sure, but there aren’t many more problems with this team, and it should also be noted that Liam has the highest points allowed all season. Managing a .500 record with 2 suspended players, an injured QB, and the worst point-scoring luck should be celebrated. Let’s just hope this big O can last the rest of the season.
blurbs.nick-dakshots-at-the-hampton-inn: First down week in a while for Nick sees him slide down the rankings. Nick has been on a bit of a tear ever since he got shelled by my team in rivalry week, but this team has been putting a lot of band-aids on axe wounds. The WR depth past Chase is horrendous, and there’s no consistency among the RBs past Kyren, who himself hasn’t been at his best. Eventually, the going might get tough for Nick’s team, seeing as how this is the first season in ages where he has good points scored luck (lowest PA in the league so far). But for now, we should celebrate the victories, and hope the core of Warren, Prescott, and Chase can carry the team to more. Because if not, big yikes.
blurbs.xander-he-bleeds-pink: Now we’re getting to the good teams, the true championship contenders. Xander has seen a 2-week skid, which deservedly sees his team fall down the ranks, but don’t let that fool you. He’s got the number 1 TE, number 1 RB, a top QB, and apparently a bunch of solid flex options. I mean hell, two of his players scored 0 points this week and he still nearly beat the median! Even with all of the injuries dealt to this team, it has persevered as a true contender. Now, Xander doesn’t really know what he’s doing, and he didn’t even draft this team himself, so I’d imagine there’s a good chance this all falls apart, but hey we’re partying for now! That iceberg is wayyyyy in the distance, we don’t need to avert course yet!
blurbs.connor-new-year-chris-leak: Those wax wings aren’t melting at all; Connor’s team is starting to get back on track. It’s not all sunshine and roses, since Connor keeps starting the wrong QB each week, and maybe we should start worrying about Chuba and Cook not playing super well lately, but this is a solid playoff team with real championship upside. Is me complimenting his team just flattering Connor and buttering him up so he’s inclined to join our dogshit softball team next year? Who’s to say, no one can ever really know. But what we do know is that this team is going to be a problem for opponents the rest of the season.
blurbs.alex-she-maye-gibbs-me-head: Call me biased all you want, this team is GOOD. I mean hell, I scored 20+ more points than every other team this week, except the one damn team I faced! Even with major injuries to important players, my team has still found ways to produce every week, and the outlook for the rest of the year is damn good. There’s probably some fable or old tale about how this kind of excessive hubris I’m displaying is actually the folly of man, and will eventually lead to my demise, but I’m choosing to ignore that in favor of winning games and scoring points (Don’t forget I laced a single at Sunday night softball too 😉).
blurbs.cameron-scott-hanson-s-protege: I had this team TENTH in the original draft rankings. Hand up, that’s on me gang. Maybe I let my McCaffrey biases get to me after he brutally bent me over last season, but this team has just been near-perfect to start the year. I’d definitely be nervous that this won’t hold: CMC and Jacobs are old and receiving a bunch of volume, apart from Egbuka the WRs show no consistency and Egbuka himself is battling injury, and Kyle Pitts is Kyle Pitts; the house of cards could come toppling down at any moment. But, I’ve been doubting this team all year, and Cam’s team continues to surprise me. So maybe this team is the 2025 Colts, and despite all odds is one of the greatest offenses of this century. I guess it’s time for me to buy in.

midseason-7.intro: The report cards are back with a vengeance. Since the rankings more or less look like the standings as the season progresses, it’s more appropriate to assess how we got here and how things have fared so far for each team. The rankings reflect record and recent trends, while the midterm grades reflect both what we’ve seen so far and my confidence in your team going forward. Hope that makes sense, and if not, maybe you’re just not smart enough to understand it.

week-8.label: Week 8

blurbs.matt-the-team-formerly-known-as-jeanty-i: After I claimed that Matt’s team might not be dogshit two weeks ago, he’s been easily the most dogshit team in the league. Jeanty hasn’t helped, Nico is hurt, the WRs, TE, and QB don’t play consistent at all, and the team name still makes no sense. Ladd is finally decent, though. So there’s that.
blurbs.austin-cyborg-squad: The long-term outlook for this team is still not the greatest, but you have to respect he’s putting in the effort to keep this season alive. Getting 3 solid starters out of Derrick Henry is probably a huge positive for Austin’s team, and this is his first 2-0 week since week 1. Will this sustain, or is this a bit like when we started the 3rd inning of our softball game only down 2-0, and the hope is unfounded, as it’s too little too late?
blurbs.rocco-team-of-bums-v8: Well, back to losing ways for Rocco’s team after a quick reprieve. I mean, this running back room is fucking putrid, half the team absolutely blows, and his only good players are tight ends. Things should be looking up from this week after all these byes, but if he can’t start getting wins soon we might start seeing Rocco focus a lot more on music than fantasy.
blurbs.tyler-team-strong-2025: It’s just Ty’s luck that he lost vs. median by half a point, but things may finally be looking up soon. Bucky is coming back, Goedert is actually great somehow, and Barkley finally had a 100-yard game. I don’t think Ty puts enough effort into fantasy to care about these things, or even read these rankings, so maybe I shouldn’t care too much about what I say here. Someone let Ty know I moved his team up two spots in the rankings.
blurbs.nick-dakshots-at-the-hampton-inn: I really can’t make heads or tails of Nick’s team. I guess this was just a tough week since lots of players were on a bye, but this was just dogshit. Two total players in double digits, which was as many that scored under 1.5, including a goose egg from Jeudy in a game that favored passing. Truly, it can only go up from here. Until Chase’s bye in a couple of weeks, in which case it might just go right back down.
blurbs.steven-i-am-a-stupid-idiot: It sucks for Steven that the six teams ahead of him have just been better, and also project to be better for the rest of the season, because his team deserves to be higher with how hot they’ve been. Add in the Derrick Henry trade and Puka return with recent performances and it’s easy to start to believe. Was he a completely BS OPI call vs. Slayton away from losing to me and going down the rankings further? Sure, but I’m not salty at all. Please don’t put in the newspaper that I’m salty.
blurbs.richard-the-pollard-express: Maybe it’s actually weird to name your team after your worst starting player, but the Pollard Express is back on the tracks. I keep hating on this team, because it’s providing a lot of cognitive dissonance to me that they keep proving me wrong, but there’s something plucky about them. Maybe things will turn south soon, since this team has experienced zero injuries at all, and virtually zero bye weeks have passed for every impactful player on this team. But despite the rest of season outlook being kind of murky, maybe this team can just shithouse their way into a playoff spot. And who knows what can happen from there?
blurbs.xander-he-bleeds-pink: What a southward turn for Xander’s team. Even with Allen and Taylor combining for nearly 60 points, he barely made it vs. the median, and had two players get zero points. There’s probably reason to be optimistic going forward, but the starting lineup past the first few guys is kinda bleak. I guess I was just looking at this team through the rose-colored glasses, created and obscured by the manager’s pink blood. If anything happens to Taylor, get the prayer circle out.

Imagine a photoshopped video of me in a convertible in Dallas, and instead of Jackie O trying to put JFK’s brains back into his head out of shock, it’s me trying to put Cam Skattebo’s ankle back into place, while crying profusely.*

blurbs.liam-rasheez-nuts: I was never wrong about Liam’s team — I was just early! If Bijan doesn’t perform, elite RB Breece Hall will. If Bill Merritt sucks, then league-winner Rashee Rice will step up. If Jayden Daniels is hurt, waiver pickup Jordan Love will fill in for him. In rain, sleet, or snow, this team is gritty and they’re playing for each other. We’ll see if this can hold, but the nuts are SWELLING with overconfidence. Mandingo type shit.
blurbs.cameron-scott-hanson-s-protege: The shoe may be finally beginning to drop for Cam’s team. Instead of combining for 40, McCaffrey and Jacobs combined for 20.3, which really throws this team off its rhythm. Is it concerning that in a week with limited byes, the team can’t hold up to pedestrian weeks from its best two players? Maybe, but everything else has worked alright so far, so maybe it’s just fine, and nothing ever happens and this won’t matter.
blurbs.connor-new-year-chris-leak: He took a multi-week hiatus, but as soon as Connor came back into the Florida air he reclaimed his spot atop the power rankings. Sure, it might not be sustainable to expect James Cook to run for over 200 yards every week, but the outlook for the rest of the season is as good as it gets. Every major player has avoided or already recovered from injury, and is now already past their bye. It’s hard finding a true weakness here, maybe tight end? Maybe depth? Or maybe Connor will just go back to back, and all of this is an exercise in futility. Who truly knows?

week-8.intro: The midseason report cards were already handed out, so now we’re in the dog days of the season. As such, the power rankings will move to biweekly, as they did last year. There’s only so much to say every week once teams truly form and there’s only so far the rankings can deviate from the actual standings. This also allows me to get a small break each week, so I want to do it. Feel free to fill the gap with any content about the league, should you feel so inspired; I can’t just keep carrying this whole thing on my back.

week-9-10.label: Weeks 9 & 10

blurbs.austin-cyborg-squad: Oof. There really isn’t much more to say than that. Two games behind all of the other bad teams in the league, and two straight weeks where your BEST performance is being the second-lowest scoring team of the week. It’s a good thing I still have the sauce from this year, I can bring it to our next D&D session so you can train your body for next year’s trip. I guess I’ll try to talk about Austin in some type of positive light: your Halloween party was very fun and I enjoyed all the themed decorations. That’s really all I got.
blurbs.tyler-team-strong-2025: It’s really saying something that there’s probably a large gap between Ty’s team and last place right now, because his team so far is not convincing. We’re ten weeks in and he’s only beaten the median three times. Two weeks ago I said we should be excited for Bucky to come back, and he’s still not healthy. Ty’s shuffling between crappy waiver wire QBs and starting Ty Johnson as his RB2. At least while he was watching his team put up a putrid performance this week, he got to watch the best President in our nation’s history do some play-by-play commentary in the Detroit-Washington game. That probably lifted Ty’s spirits a bit.
blurbs.matt-the-team-formerly-known-as-jeanty-i: We’re finally seeing some consistency with Matt’s team, and he’s out of the league’s basement. Am I convinced that these performances can continue? …No. But, are things finally starting to look up for this team’s star players? …Also no, we can’t trust virtually any of them to either stay healthy or perform consistently. BUT, will we see this team have a late-season rally and find their way into the 6 seed? …Again, probably no, but we do have to appreciate the effort.
blurbs.liam-rasheez-nuts: Alright, I think I finally have to take my L on Liam’s team. He’s gonna say something like “9 is bull” in the chat, but it’s not just the 0-4 last two weeks that inspire this ranking, it’s the way we got here. Two straight weeks where the best score was not even 82 points. In both losses, Liam’s opponent couldn’t win vs. the median, and Liam’s team wasn’t even close to winning. I mean the injuries to Daniels and Wilson plus the Bijan underperformances have really exposed the nuts for who they are: shriveled, small, and fraudulent. (I play Liam this week. Massive blowout in his favor incoming?)
blurbs.steven-i-am-a-stupid-idiot: Steven’s team is just repeating what they’ve done all season long: score a bunch one week, and then very little the next. It is kind of nice, in a way, that there’s so much consistency within the inconsistency. We probably shouldn’t know what to expect from this team this week, but then know exactly what to expect next week based on this week’s performance. It must be freeing, to just have no idea what to expect every week. To cap all of this weirdness off, the second I start believing Daniel Jones can be good, he turns back into a pumpkin. C’est la vie.
blurbs.rocco-team-of-bums-v8: What the fuck has gotten into this team all of a sudden? Maybe this is just a response to having bum ass BTJ off the roster, and the locker room is responding positively to that? McBride is actually giving a positional advantage each week, Drake London is playing out of his mind, and Bo is stepping up to be a leader. We’ll see if this is just a random mid-season spike out of nowhere, and things will go back to normal soon, but man you gotta love the fight in this team. Almost in the top 6 of the power rankings for the first time since the draft, you gotta love it.
blurbs.nick-dakshots-at-the-hampton-inn: Nick’s team is 6th in the rankings, with as many wins as he has losses in both his head-to-head record and his median record, and is 8th in points scored. It feels fitting to have him ranked as appropriately mid as his team has performed so far. I guess I’d say brighter days are ahead for this team, since some injuries should be clearing up and most of the important players’ bye weeks are out of the way. But he’ll probably finish 14-14 and maybe sneak his way into the playoffs, regardless of most of these other things. So who even cares?
blurbs.alex-she-maye-gibbs-me-head: It’s a shame that wins are more important than points, because my team is great at scoring points, but really bad at getting wins. I’m not *too* worried (yet) since every important bye is over and I should be getting some players back from injury soon. But man it’d just be nice to not have the most points allowed in the league. I guess this is karma for last year’s team that was dogshit but had the least points allowed? I’m also projected for 123 this week against Liam so I’m ready for the most disappointing 89-point performance in our league’s history.
blurbs.richard-the-pollard-express: The weather is getting colder, and the Pollard Express keeps trudging through the ice and snow toward its eventual end goal. A bit of a skid in week 9, for sure, but they rebounded nicely last week even with some important bye weeks impeding them. Now, the question then remains, is this team actually good, and can this sustain? And I’m not sure I have a definitive answer for that yet. But they keep getting wins, which is far more important than being “good.” So honestly, does it matter?
blurbs.connor-new-year-chris-leak: Connor does keep racking up the wins, so maybe I should give his team more respect, but it was pointed out to me by Matt that we’re 10 whole weeks into the season and Connor has 90 less points allowed than the next lowest team, and has faced a 90-point scorer just 4 times this season. So, maybe I should have a lot less faith in this team’s playoff hopes. But Connor’s team keeps winning, so I have to rank him highly in the name of journalistic integrity. I’ll just do it grumpily, with a frown on my face.
blurbs.xander-he-bleeds-pink: Oh baby, we are SO back. Is Jonathan Taylor the best player of all time? Xander’s sources are saying yes. Now, is it worrying that the one week Taylor underperforms is also the week where Xander has one of his worst performances? Maybe, so maybe that means during his bye this week Xander might as well forfeit his matchup. But the team is starting to click once again, just like the beginning of the year, and just maybe we might see a Smith brother holding the championship belt for the first time since Austin first bought it to give to me (humblebrag).
blurbs.cameron-scott-hanson-s-protege: Who else could it be? Literally everything is working for Cam’s team right now. It doesn’t matter who underperforms, or who gets hurt, because the rest of the team is picking up the slack. I said the shoe might drop for this team, and I gotta just admit I was wrong. This is a championship contender through and through, and that’s with Marvin Harrison on the team! Not much else to say other than this goes to show that your team staying healthy all year is arguably more important than every other aspect of fantasy, as shown by this team’s continual dominance.

week-9-10.intro: Apologies for the first off week of the season; I hope Xander’s WAR rankings were enough to tide everyone over. We’re back though, yet another week to talk about how shit Austin’s team is and hear me complain about stupid shit.

week-11-12.label: Weeks 11 & 12

blurbs.matt-the-team-formerly-known-as-jeanty-i: This team has had its ups and downs all year, but really, it’s been mostly downs — which is fitting, because that’s the syndrome I’d use to describe how Matt’s players have been playing lately. Only Joe Burrow has been a major injury for this team, and that production has been largely subsidised by Jaxson Dart anyway, so really this team is completely healthy and just big mega dookie ass. Hilariously, Matt is only two spots out of a playoff spot, so maybe he can turn things around and do the impossible. But, I don’t think anyone believes he can, least of all Matt himself. Just prepare your anus for the liquid shits that come with extremely hot wings.
blurbs.austin-cyborg-squad: Just as we thought this team was cruising to the worst record in league history, after Lamar has been hurt and playing like shit and Laporta is likely out for the year, they crawl their way back for one last fight. I mean, two median wins in a row, and with 4 wins possible remaining this team is actually not even eliminated from the playoffs yet. It probably won’t lead to anything, but fuck, imagine if it does! How hilarious would that be?
blurbs.rocco-team-of-bums-v8: Wow man. We were feeling so good. We were feeling like we might even find our way into a playoff spot! We were so close, too. And then London had to get himself hurt and fuck everything up, didn’t he? Such is life on the Rocco fantasy football experience. Technically he’s still in it, being only two games back from Liam in the 6th spot, but does anyone believe Rocco can actually do it? I mean, fuck, he unironically played Tyler fucking Shough this week. That’s got to be a new low for this league, right?
blurbs.tyler-team-strong-2025: After how poorly the season started (and has been for most of the year), this team is one win out of a playoff spot. Losing both your 2nd and 3rd round picks for extended time, plus your 1st round pick being extremely mid, will ruin a lot of confidence you have in your team. But Davante keeps scoring, and Bucky should be back soon, so there’s legitimately reason to be optimistic. Are we actually going to see Team Strong get over the hump and find their way into the playoffs? Probably not, but why not have some fun and believe in miracles?
blurbs.nick-dakshots-at-the-hampton-inn:
All of these teams are shit. I don’t want to rank any of them 6th and taint the other playoff teams with their presence. And I don’t want to rank any of them 7th either, because that implies they’re just barely out of the playoffs. You all deserve to be 8th, with a full spot between you and the last playoff berth, and it disgusts me that we might have a team with a losing record representing our 6th seed in the playoffs.

Nick gets his 1st-round pick back this week, and that guy’s QB is healthy again, so maybe things look up. But Hampton is still hurt and probably just done for the year, he has no consistency elsewhere in the lineup, and he just put up the worst score the entire league has seen this season, so is there anything to really cheer for?

Steven at BEST can be .500, has put up three straight sub-90-point weeks, and lost Tee Higgins for the foreseeable future. Somehow he has a nearly 30% chance to make the playoffs according to the fantasy app, but seeing as his best player is getting taken out of the game every two plays for Chuba Hubbard, I think that chance is too high.

Liam finally turned it around last week, and the momentum is finally in his favor. But the three weeks before that he was 7th, 11th, and 12th in the median standings, and I don’t think it’s reasonable to expect Hunter Henry and WanDale Robinson to combine for 50 points each week. It’s looking like he’ll be the guy to get into that final spot, at least for now, but instead of a triumphant return to glory, it’ll look more like tripping and falling over the finish line.

These teams disgust me, and it disgusts me even more that one of them will have a legitimate chance at winning the championship. And maybe even two, depending on how Richard’s final two weeks go. Ugh.
blurbs.richard-the-pollard-express: Imagine being in a race, tripping and falling flat on your face, getting up, and then doing it again. Then you look back and somehow you’ve GAINED on your fellow competitors. That’s what’s happening with Rich right now; a bad two-week skid has not seen him falter in the standings one bit. One more 2-0 week will surely clinch the playoffs, and this was a week with no Achane or Waddle so I gotta cut Richard a little slack here, 8th in points considering that factor isn’t too awful. The Pollard Express is trudging along the snow and ice, confident they can make the final stretch. But do they have what it takes to win the race?
blurbs.connor-new-year-chris-leak: The points allowed luck is finally catching up to Connor a bit here, but it seems to be too little too late. Any win or combo of Nick and Liam loss will see him clinch the fourth playoff spot, so we’re not really stressing there. But it should again be noted that Connor’s median record in the past month or so has been concerning, to say the least. Thankfully he finally broke 100 for the first time in ages this week, because otherwise we’d be heading into the playoffs against some real juggernauts with zero confidence. Although everything seems to work out for Connor in life, so he probably has zero reason to be worried and will coast to back-to-back titles. Here’s to hoping he sees SOME adversity.
blurbs.alex-she-maye-gibbs-me-head: Vibes are extremely high right now. A nice 4-0 two-week stretch to clinch the playoffs, Gibbs and JSN combined for like 83 points last week, North London is red, and I’m consistently getting laid. I don’t even care that I’m not in first, I’m just vibing at levels previously thought impossible. You guys have fun fighting for who might get some money if people don’t eat their wings, I’ve got bigger fish to fry.
blurbs.cameron-scott-hanson-s-protege: It sucks for Cam that a one-week skid sees him slide down the rankings, but the margins are thin at the top, and you have to be at your best to retain the spot on the throne. We’re still feeling great though, I mean the old RB experiment has worked even better than anyone could’ve expected, and maybe we just want Emmanuel Wilson to take over the reins for the rest of the season! No more stress, the playoff spot has been clinched, and we might still find our way into first place.
blurbs.xander-he-bleeds-pink: Xander has been in and out of the top spot all season, but if recent performances are any indication, it looks like he’s here to stay. Taylor and Allen have been the X-factors (pardon the “X” pun) for this team all year, so it’s a bit frightening for the rest of us contenders that in a week where they combine for 15 points Xander still tops 100. I don’t think I’ve mentioned once this year just how good George Pickens has been for this team, but fuck he might be the Cowboys’ best receiver! All this to say, if this keeps up, the Machine 2.5 may be validated in its process after this year’s playoffs.

week-11-12.intro: There are two weeks remaining in the season, which means this is the penultimate power rankings of 2025. Since we’re really in the thick of it, and the regular season is about to end, it’s only fitting we discuss the one topic at the forefront of everyone’s minds: PLAYOFFS.

playoff-14.label: Playoff Predictor

blurbs.austin-cyborg-squad: It’s only fitting that the guy who spent the final week of the season golfing and not checking his lineup would end up all the way down here at the bottom. The only team to not break double-digit wins, the only team to not score at least 1200 points in the regular season, the only team to have clinched five wings, and the reigning wing champion; he simply has to be the wing favorite going into the playoffs. Austin only has one player on his team that’s even top 12 in their respective position, so it’s not like he has much to look forward to in these next three weeks either. We’ve yet to see last place in the regular season be last place in the playoffs, and we’re in the Double Jeopardy portion of the season now; will we see Austin double up his wing count?
blurbs.tyler-team-strong-2025: In any normal year, Ty would have probably seen himself much closer to last place than he actually was; his 2nd-round pick has barely played, his 3rd-round pick tore his ACL in like week 4, and his 1st-round pick has been arguably the worst 1st-rounder this season. So, the fact that he’s in second-to-last, and the fact that he hasn’t broken 100 points since week 9 and has only one week all season where he scored more than 107, means we have to rank his wing chances decently high. At least we know he’d want to give Elijah good content, and wouldn’t bitch out of eating the wings. So maybe we should root for him to fail? Not like it’d be hard.
blurbs.matt-the-team-formerly-known-as-jeanty-i: Matt really turned it around right at the tail end of this season. Unfortunately, it wasn’t nearly enough to make the playoffs (I mean hell, it was barely enough to escape last place) but it does leave us decently optimistic heading into this season’s Toilet Bowl. It is funny that this team has had virtually zero meaningful injuries, and arguably the highest value pick in the draft in an 8th-round Javonte Williams, and we’re still way down here at the bottom. Maybe Matt’s drafting strategy of “do absolutely zero research and pick based off of vibes” has finally caught up to him? Although he’s beaten the median in 3 of the last 5 weeks, so maybe things are actually perfectly fine, and there’s nothing to worry about… right?
blurbs.steven-i-am-a-stupid-idiot: Wow, was Steven right on the money when he said his trades would ruin his season or what? I know we should feel better about this team heading into this Toilet Bowl but fuck, I just can’t get that last week out of my head. Had Steven’s team scored somewhere around 120 points, he might have snuck his way into the playoffs, but he couldn’t even get half of that total. Steven hasn’t even broken 90 points since week 9, so maybe this whole “playoff hopeful” thing he had going for him was actually a complete farce. It’s probably karmically just that he ends up in this spot, vying yet again to not eat the wings (which he didn’t even do last year, so maybe this doesn’t even matter).
blurbs.rocco-team-of-bums-v8: Rocco’s team has been at or around the bottom all season, so imagine my surprise when I found out he was not that far off of making the playoffs when all was said and done. It was more of a backdoor cover than a true playoff fight, but still, ending in 8th place in the regular season is probably better than everyone, including Rocco, expected after his abysmal start. Since week 6, Rocco has actually been a decently consistent scorer (with only 3 out of 9 weeks below 90 and 1 out of 9 below 84) and even has a winning record, so maybe it’s time to put some respect on this team. Of course, every time I start believing in Rocco’s team, they prove themselves unreliable and play like dogshit, so maybe that’s a sign he’s due to eat the wings again.
blurbs.liam-rasheez-nuts:
What a disappointing end to what looked to be a promising season. I had Liam ranked as high as the number 1 spot this season, and even up at number 3 in week 8; to end up down here slumming it with the other losers is just the worst outcome we could have ever imagined. And we were so close too; two straight high-scoring weeks to get us back to .500 and give us a chance to make it in the final week, only to completely shit the bed in hilarious fashion. This team, after all of its trials and tribulations, probably shouldn’t be a true wing contender. But we DID just see earlier in the season a three-week skid where Liam’s top score was 82 points, so maybe we should be decently worried?



Playoff Teams
blurbs.connor-new-year-chris-leak: Our reigning champion started the season red-hot, only losing 1 game in the first 4 weeks and constantly finding himself atop the power rankings. Since those first 4 weeks, Connor’s team has scored over 100 points just 3 times out of 10, and he won vs. the median only 4 times. Just when we thought we might see a repeat champion, this team has grinded to a screeching halt, and every player we thought was good turned out to be shit and unreliable. I mean, shit, he’s 8th in total points, how is he fighting for the same title that the rest of us are?
blurbs.nick-dakshots-at-the-hampton-inn: It was a super up-and-down season for Nick’s team, but in the end, the Dakshots have found their way into the playoffs. Key player Omarion Hampton is FINALLY back, we’ve purged our roster of the traitorous and untrustworthy DJ Moore, and Nick may be feeling optimistic for once. Sure, there’s very little consistency this year with Nick’s team; I mean I don’t know that there’s even one player that I can trust would give me 15 on a week-to-week basis. But you could convince yourself that this team could go all the way; theoretically there are LOTS of explosive players on this roster, just waiting to break out and have their league-winning games. It just all needs to come together now, when it rarely has all season. Easy.
blurbs.richard-the-pollard-express: After a weird start, and a few roadblocks along the way, the train has been chugging along very smoothly in the latter half of the season. Fitting to name the team after the Polar Express, because once the weather started getting more icy and snowy, Richard’s team got better and better. After the first four weeks where we didn’t break 100 even once, this team has been a surprisingly consistent 100-point scorer, with a couple of spike weeks thrown in there too. This is also the first team we’ve covered that actually has a positive record vs. the median, so maybe this is the first team with true championship potential. Or maybe the train will derail, and sink like the Titanic after colliding with an iceberg. Having your entire offense basically depend on the Miami Dolphins doesn’t seem like a good strategy during the winter months, but I’ve not really believed in this team all year, maybe I should start now.
blurbs.cameron-scott-hanson-s-protege: Cam’s fantasy history is relatively disappointing for all of the regular season wins he’s racked up; always the bridesmaid, never the bride. He was in first place for a large portion of the season, and was nearly the top-record and top-scoring team, and then these past few weeks has kind of just petered out and limped across the finish line. This team has shown us all season that, at its best, it’s a true, out-and-out championship contender. I just look at the past 4 weeks of only scoring more than 90 points one time, and having three 0-2 performances in that span, and I wonder if the team itself believes in their chances. Maybe McCaffrey, Jacobs, and Hurts can be the guys to finally lead Cam to the promised land. Or maybe we see more of the same that we’ve seen in recent weeks, and Cam falls just short once again.
blurbs.alex-she-maye-gibbs-me-head: For as much shit as I talk about this game, I feel my team has really backed it up this season. We have the top record and we were less than a point off of being the first-place team, and two of the last three weeks have been over 140-point weeks. Granted, maybe we shouldn’t expect Gibbs to score three touchdowns every game, and two of my best players in Tee Higgins and CeeDee Lamb are likely out with concussions in this first playoff week (a massive blow). But call me crazy, I still have faith this team is getting red hot at the right time. All season I believed we’ve been among the favorites, and all season I’ve been proven right. Can Gibbs, JSN, and Maye carry me to glory? I really fuckin hope so, because last time I got second place that sucked ass.
blurbs.xander-he-bleeds-pink: Xander has been top of the standings, the power rankings, and the point total for quite a bit of this season, so it’s only fitting he finds himself at the top of the championship chances. We’re a bit worried about how the Daniel Jones injury affects our best player in Taylor, and maybe we can’t expect old guys like Jones, Deebo, Jakobi, or Kittle to really make a difference for us against the best of the best. But we’ve been doing it all season, and we have Josh Allen on our team, who can go for 50 in any given week. We haven’t been stopped yet, so why think we’ll be stopped now? This team is the favorite until proven otherwise. Which may be immediately, but still, have some faith.

playoff-14.intro:
We’ve now officially made it to the final stretch - it’s playoff time. Over the next three weeks, six teams will turn to one as we fight for arguably our hardest-to-predict championship in league history. And also, six shitty teams will do everything possible to not be the most shitty team, and avoid another five wings added to their punishment (I say “another” five because we already know who the favorite to get them is). Each team will have a playoff prediction percentage next to their name; percentage of championship for playoff teams, and percentage of wings for Toilet Bowl teams. Is this number completely arbitrary and basically just based on vibes? Yes, but don’t let that stop you from using it against me if you end up winning, or something. Teams are sorted by regular season standings, not power rankings or playoff chances.

retrospective.label: Season Retrospective

blurbs.austin-cyborg-squad:
What I wrote in September, about the Machine breaking halfway through the draft: “Maybe you should just take this as an omen, Aug.” Boy, could that not have been more correct.

Doing these rankings can be a pain in the ass sometimes, since there are always multiple teams you could justify putting in every single spot. Then, every so often, a gem like Austin’s team comes around, and it makes my job just that little bit easier knowing I don’t have to work hard for at least this one. This one is nice. It is ultimately fitting and just that the team who was 12th in the beginning, midpoint, and end rankings, and also the regular season standings, ends up as our playoff loser. It wouldn’t have felt right any other way. The team’s best player was a WR who scored 3 total touchdowns on the season.

This season will not be remembered fondly, and the most impactful moves made were the ones made not by a machine, but by the man himself. Trading away Derrick Henry for three starters seemed okay at the time, but it didn’t stop Austin from getting last place in the regular season, and Henry’s playoff performances likely would have seen Austin escape the doubling of his last-place punishment. On top of that, Austin spent almost 100% of his FAAB on Tre Tucker, and ended up starting him for the majority of the season. Since Tucker’s 36.9-point performance in week 3, he scored double-digit points one time, and was the WR67 (👀) in points per game. The moves were bad, the team was consistently at the bottom of the league, and Austin got what he deserved. At least the season wasn’t the WORST it could have been, since he didn’t have to give his cold hard cash to his bitter rival and brother… right?
blurbs.tyler-team-strong-2025:
What I wrote in September: “I think it’s extremely realistic to expect a good portion of his team to be injured for a lot of the season, due to both Ty’s fantasy luck and the average age and usage of his players.” Bucky Irving missed 7 games. Tyreek Hill missed 13 games. Ty’s original starting QB Justin Fields missed 1, was benched, came back, was benched again, and is now on IR to end the year. Davante Adams, Ty’s only decent player, ended the season hurt too. I have to say, I think I’m 2 for 2 on September predictions.

Tyler benefitted greatly from Austin’s team’s ineptitude, because otherwise this season was nothing short of a disaster for him. It’s hard to make a retrospective “what went wrong” assertion about a team that didn’t make a trade and basically stayed exactly the same since draft day, but I think what I outlined in the first paragraph sums it all up; injuries derailed this team early. Almost immediately into the season, Ty was fighting for his life having to deal with missing out on Irving and Hill, and Saquon was completely pedestrian compared to last season. Maybe Ty should’ve been shaking it up more, and made a couple of trades along the way? I’m not sure for who, but it kinda feels like he took strike one and then just went down looking. Which, admittedly, gave him the same fate as the other 8 of us who both didn’t win and didn’t get last, so maybe it’s fine.
blurbs.matt-the-team-formerly-known-as-jeanty-i:
What I wrote in September: “...wait he got Cooper Kupp and Javonte Williams and both will play important roles for him this season? And then I was like, Joe Burrow in the 4th round? Nevermind, I’m good. Also, he didn’t get George Kittle for the first time in 3-4 years. That might be a sign that his team will underperform.” A big swing and a miss on Javonte, but otherwise generally correct (although not exactly genius-level foresight to think that Kupp was going to be bad this year). Maybe George Kittle is the glue that held this team together — after all, he was a fantasy champion this year.

Here’s another team that was a beneficiary of Austin’s generational suckage, because virtually every draft pick underperformed, and every week we saw them fighting for last place. I had a few players in mind for this team’s worst player; Ashton Jeanty in the first round was a fucking massive disappointment on one of the more putrid offenses we’ve seen in the 21st century who basically had like 3 good weeks out of 17, and Joe Burrow was a bad fantasy QB for a couple of weeks and then injured himself for three full months, so he was a complete sunk cost about a month in. But, the title had to go to Ladd McConkey, who was basically a complete nothing for Matt’s team all season, despite being drafted extremely highly and being placed in the starting lineup virtually every week. I felt pretty whatever about this team when we left the draft, and I think that captures the emotion they conveyed all season; they were truly a whatever team. Maybe things are different with a better first-round pick, or an Amon-Ra over Collins in the 2nd round, or something, I don’t know. Another team with zero trades that went down looking, I’m sensing a pattern here.
blurbs.steven-i-am-a-stupid-idiot:
What I wrote in September: “Last year, Steven took four WRs before taking his first RB, and drafted Zamir White as his starting RB2. This year, he learned a bit from his mistakes, only drafting three WRs before taking his first RB. It might not seem like much, but every journey begins with just a single step.” Again, an easy prediction to hit on, that this team would be better than last year’s last-place team, but I’ll take the wins where I can get them.

I was very hopeful about this team heading into the season, ranking them as the 2nd-best team post draft. And there were times this season where that came to fruition, and Steven would have a roster putting up 140 or 150-point weeks. But fantasy requires a bit more consistency, and unfortunately the second we saw some from Steven it was too little too late.

Puka was the obvious bright spot on a team that suffered many injuries and many crushing defeats. I mean, he was probably on many championship rosters, and would have been on Steven’s too had he made the playoffs. An incredible run by an incredible player. For worst player, I considered a few before ultimately landing on Rome, but I do want to give a special shoutout to Calvin Ridley, who is arguably the worst 5th-round pick this league has ever seen. A truly generational waste of space on Steven’s roster.

Unlike the previous two teams, Steven actually made too MANY trades, rather than too few. Had he not been persuaded to trade Tee Higgins for Rome Odunze (a trade I would defend at the time, since it made sense for both me and him regarding our teams’ present outlooks), he’d be celebrating a championship, since he outscored everyone else in the league during the playoffs (Well, maybe this isn’t true, I haven’t checked this myself. Steven has said that this is what cost him a playoff spot and I’m choosing to believe him. If this is wrong, yell at him.). The Derrick Henry and Chris Olave trades were masterful and helped Steven not secure last, and even in a season where things immediately went haywire with Nabers’s injury, Steven persevered. It’s too bad none of that really mattered though. Sorry Steve.
blurbs.rocco-team-of-bums-v8:
What I wrote in September: “Rocco went in only focusing on vibes and not worrying about fantasy analysis or any of that bullshit, and he ended up scooping up good value and building a solid foundation to a good team. Now, the average age of his starting RBs is 29, but we’ll just push that to the side and pretend we didn’t see it.” 

The RBs were among the biggest problems with this team, as expected. Who knew taking a 30-year-old Alvin Kamara leading a bad offense to be your top RB would be a bad idea? Bo Nix kind of put it together, but he wasn’t exactly a world beater either. This team suffered through lots of inconsistencies throughout the year. Granted, Rocco was a very good manager, and did what he could to salvage a poor draft. He traded away CeeDee Lamb for Drake London when he was hurt, which worked great, then traded London for Olave when HE was hurt, which worked out even better. He filled out the RB slots on his team and did everything he could to remain competitive, which you have to applaud. I’d throw Rocco’s hat in the ring for the Coach of the Year award.

I had high hopes for this team. Sure, I wasn’t in LOVE with the entirety of the roster, but it was well-constructed. Unfortunately, everything about this team mostly comes down to one man, and that’s Brian Thomas. After having a top-10 rookie pass catching season of all time, revamped with a dynamo head coach and new WR mates around him, he basically proved last season was a complete fluke and shit the bed at virtually every opportunity this year. Having a second-round pick perform this poorly is only ever going to spell disaster for your team, so you can make as many savvy moves as you’d like to salvage things, it just wasn’t enough. At least we went down swinging, right?
blurbs.liam-rasheez-nuts:
What I wrote in September: “Liam passed up on the number one player, took two Jets players back-to-back, and ended up with two guys suspended for a total of nine games. I’m not sure he knows exactly how he’s gonna navigate that, but let’s just look at the good QB and top-end talent and kinda distract ourselves from those red flags; it’ll probably work out somehow.” Well, I was wrong about the QB being good, and that Liam passing on the number one player would be a mistake, and that it’d probably work out somehow. But at least I called the Jets thing.

Liam had one of the more tumultuous seasons of anyone in our league. I don’t think anyone experienced the highs and lows quite like him. I mean there was a point in this year where I looked at his roster and was like, fuck, this is arguably the best team in the league. I ranked him as the number 1 team in the Power Rankings at some point this year, and he seemed a true playoff contender with about a month to go. Daniels was a massive bust, sure, and the Jets looked like they were getting worse, but it seemed like things were looking up with Addison and Rashee being back from suspension and Bijan tearing it up. 

I distinctly remember plugging our league’s rosters into a “player value” calculator in like, week 11, so right in the throes of the playoff hunt, and Liam’s team was very firmly in 2nd place. And then I guess his team just collapsed. He likes to blame me for correctly pointing out that there were over 78% of scenarios in which his team clinched a playoff berth in the final week of the season, but we know that’s just him coping and deflecting from his own failures. I mean, what did I do, tell him he had a good chance? And that’s my fault?

Drafting multiple Jets players was bad. Basically deleting your 3rd-round pick was bad. We haven’t even gotten to AJ Brown, who was also a giant bust in the 2nd round, which was also bad. Bill Croskey-Merritt, I mean what the fuck happened with him, he went like 10 weeks without a touchdown. Honestly, it was kind of miraculous that Liam even ended as close to making the playoffs as he did. I think that’s something to hang your hat on, at least.
blurbs.connor-new-year-chris-leak:
What I wrote in September: ““Oooh look at me, I’m Connor, I just had an amazing wedding with all of my friends and family and now I’m travelling the world with my wife who loves me and I just won fantasy last year and I had the best draft this year despite the fact that I was drafting from a hotel in southwestern Africa” man fuck you.” I stand by that.

Connor’s team turned from the best in the league, to one of the worst in the league, to the most fraudulent in the league, to the championship favorites, to the eventual runners up, just single-digit points away from winning it all. I mean I don’t even think he could have predicted how close he ended up getting, and also how much he fell off from week 15 to the finale. A bizarre ride the entire way that truly encapsulates fantasy football at its best. 

Up until the playoffs, Connor’s team was 8th in total points and had more median losses than wins in the previous 10 weeks. And, taking away week 15, the trend of underperforming relative to expectations continued for this team. It’s just that an absolutely nuclear, incredibly special, borderline unprecedented playoff round 1 performance catapulted this team from playoff frauds to championship hopefuls in an instant. I don’t think the players even knew what to do when they got to that point, which could explain the eventual collapse.

In trying to find this team’s worst or most disappointing player, we could talk about Justin Jefferson and how he proved he is not in fact QB-proof and from week 10 onward he’s had one game where he surpassed double digit fantasy points. Or we could talk about 4th-round pick Chuba Hubbard getting hurt and then immediately losing his starting job to a guy who had 200+ scrimmage yards in back-to-back games. But, when discussing this season, there’s really one failure that stands above them all, and that’s the Chris Olave for Drake London trade that ultimately ruined Connor’s championship hopes. I respect what Connor did here, attempting to move a good WR and some depth for a top-5 option to strengthen the roster for the playoffs. But boy did it not work. Olave was the WR2 from week 13 to week 17, only behind Puka Nacua, and London only played 2 games in that span and amassed a total of 5.1 points, including the final Monday Night Football game of the season where Connor needed 12 points and London couldn’t even muster 1. Just brutal.

I hope this is a season that Connor will remember fondly; a great start with a great draft followed by an improbable playoff run and eventual podium placing is still nothing to sneeze at. We’ll always have those Trevor Lawrence goal line rushing TDs at Cameron’s place, they can never take that away from us.
blurbs.nick-dakshots-at-the-hampton-inn:
What I wrote in September: “I think my main problem is everyone is just kinda fine, like there’s no inherent problem with this team, I just look at all the other teams above it and I’m like “Damn! Hell yeah!” and I look at Nick’s and I’m like “alright cool, thumbs up I guess.” A nice double in the gap.”

I can’t think of a better summation of Nick’s fantasy season than this: I ranked him 5th in the preseason rankings, 5th in the midseason rankings, 5th in the postseason rankings, and he finished as the 5th-place team in the playoffs. Like I said, a nice double in the gap. That was exemplified even further in me struggling to figure out who Nick’s “best” player was this season; I settled on Chase, who I think was the only player on Nick’s team not subject to rape threats by him, but even he was kind of just fine relative to expectations. 

We cannot talk about this year without mentioning enemy of the state DJ Moore, who was a 5th-round pick that only had 3 double-digit scoring weeks and 2 weeks inside the top 24 scoring WRs on the season, who then proceeded to score 40 points for rival playoff performer Cameron in weeks 15 and 16. Truly a scourge on Nick’s season, and I’d be surprised if he ever rostered Moore again.

It was all fun and games when I beat him in rivalry week and RIP BOZO’d him, and that might have honestly been the high point of Nick’s season. Ultimately a season and team he’d probably like to forget.
blurbs.richard-the-pollard-express:
What I wrote in September: “Is this ranking done in part because it’s funny to rank Richard’s draft this low after all the shit he talks? Yes. Is it also done in part because he has a poor WR room, a risky TE pick, a QB that hasn’t finished inside the top-10 in points per game in the last two seasons, and has the worst-ranked team according to a consensus of 110 fantasy experts? Also yes.” Listen, it was still funny to do that even though it ended up only being sort of true, so I have no regrets. I’ll admit, I was far lower than I should have been on this team immediately after the draft (something I admitted and attempted to rectify in the earlier rankings posts of the season), but some of the things that ended up working out for this team were things that even Richard didn’t expect, like Troy Franklin, Michael Pittman, and Jaylen Waddle. The RBs were mid and the QB and WRs were better, which is not what he drafted for.

The Pollard Express ultimately derailed off the tracks just short of the finish line, but after a weird and tumultuous season, I think 3rd is something nice to hang our hats on here. Metcalf was an annoying player to have as your top WR, the trio of Henderson, Brown, and Pollard were extremely inconsistent and downright bad for a majority of the season, and we had to settle on Juwan Johnson as our season’s starting TE. But, the combination of Mahomes and Achane kind of propelled Rich into a playoff spot, and the Tyreek injury meant Waddle was far more of a feature player than we ever thought he would be, so things ended up weirdly working out.

Richard is a big proponent of trading, so I was surprised/a bit disappointed to see him be more passive this year on the trade block. Maybe one solid trade could have helped consolidate some of the inconsistent talent on this roster? Can’t say anything for certain, and I don’t know much about the negotiations that went on behind the scenes that maybe almost happened. Considering how close this team was to winning the championship though, I’m sure Richard may be left lamenting what could have been.
blurbs.cameron-scott-hanson-s-protege:
What I wrote in September: “You know, I can’t say I would ever advise someone to use their first-round pick on a near-30s running back who has both degenerative bilateral Achilles Tendonitis and a torn PCL. But every time Cameron drafted CMC it has worked before, so who am I to tell him he shouldn’t?” Man fuck you. This shouldn’t have worked. Why am I the guy who had to suffer with this fuckin’ asshole last year and it just worked out perfectly for Cameron this season?

This season for Cam was almost exactly what he expected, but to the nth degree; the first three picks of Cam’s draft established a very solid floor, and allowed the rest of the players room for error in case there were weeks they didn’t perform. Now, I certainly didn’t expect CMC to be this consistent (and this healthy) all year, and I wasn’t expecting this many great games from Jacobs either, nor was I expecting Egbuka to be one of the best draft picks in fantasy for the first half of the season. All of this combined could have easily led Cam to his first championship in the modern era of the Lakewood Legends fantasy league.

However, things kind of fell apart as the season progressed. I kept mentioning how Cam’s team lacked depth, and the back-end starters inspired little confidence. This was a theme that ate away at Cam all year, missing out on first place and potentially the championship due to poor flex options. Rhamondre Stevenson, Marvin Harrison, Zach Charbonnet, Devonta Smith; all guys that really couldn’t put it together for more than a week or two at a time, and you never knew what you were getting out of them. 

The other thing that truly defined Cam’s season was in-season management; it seemed that at literally every opportunity, Cameron started the wrong player, and it cost him points/wins in the process. I don’t know if we’ve ever seen a worse manager performance regarding start/sit decisions in the league’s history. FantasyPros gives Cam a 75% start/sit accuracy for the season, which is the league’s lowest, and I think that’s what will truly eat away at Cam when he remembers this year. 

And unfortunately, the season ended with a whimper. It helps to contextualize Cameron’s playoff performance by emphasizing that his worst and least-reliable scorer, Kyle Pitts, had a 40-point performance in the first week of the playoffs, and Christian McCaffrey was the top-scoring RB in weeks 15-17, and even with those scores, Cam still couldn’t finish inside this season’s top 3 playoff performances. Maybe Cam will sit awake at night wondering what could have been, had just a few more things gone right.
blurbs.alex-she-maye-gibbs-me-head:
What I wrote in September: “There’s a world where having the best TE, a lot of high-floor, high-ceiling breakout WRs, and a potential top-tier RB makes this team a championship contender. There’s also a world where none of that happens and Drake Maye is bad and I have no RB2. Let’s take some risks, baby! The wings don’t scare me (he says, lying)!” Well, I was right that things mostly broke right for me this season, and I was, IN THEORY, a championship contender. It certainly doesn’t feel that way after our playoff performance though.

There’s a lot I could say about this team and this season, and I’m not really sure where to begin. Trading for Cam Skattebo was fun, until he got hurt. Trading for CeeDee Lamb was fun, until he completely shat the bed in the playoffs. Having Drake Maye and JSN as my team’s cornerstones was extremely fun for the year, they were awesome pretty much all of the time, and having Gibbs as a potential nuclear option just made this season all the more fun. And then I traded for Tee Higgins, and I thought MAN this is arguably the best team in the league, maybe even a super team, on paper (key words there).

Bowers as the team’s worst player seems dramatic, considering he was the TE4 when he played, but trust me when I say it never really felt that way. The Raiders couldn’t move the ball and Bowers played hurt for a month before being shut down for the next month, so he was extremely frustrating to own and I never once felt like I had a “positional advantage” at TE. Note to self, never draft a Raider ever again.

A point off of first place, arguably the best roster in the league, only to completely shit the bed immediately and be the worst team in the playoffs. This team was the true paper tigers of the season. Which is unfortunate, because most of the season was so fun, and I wish I’d be able to remember it more fondly. Oh well. There’s always next year I guess.
blurbs.xander-he-bleeds-pink:
What I wrote in September: “In a surprising twist, I actually don’t dislike this team at all. Sure, the RBs don’t inspire much confidence, but drafting strong WRs and depth while also taking a shot on an early RB and securing an elite QB and TE is really not a bad way to go about things. I think my only problem is with the RB and WR the machine picked early, but not the thought process itself. Maybe the machine started glitching out because it was making a worse team for its creator than it was for Xander?” I suppose I wasn’t too harsh on this team pre-draft, maybe what I’m learning is I should have even more hot takes and be even more outlandish with it, Stephen A style, so as to allow me to look more right or more wrong at the end of the year.

Now, we reach the final team, our best team in the regular season and our eventual gold medal winner. Carried by a draft bot that wasn’t even created by him. Having 3rd, 4th, and 6th round picks that were basically deleted for the better part of 2 months. Not even being that great at making start/sit decisions. Finishing with the worst championship performance this league has ever seen. Yet, none of that really ended up mattering, and Xander found himself atop the pile of corpses at the end of the battle; bloodied, exhausted, but victorious.

Obviously, the season is defined by Jonathan Taylor’s resurgence, and his first fully-healthy season in 4 years. However, I’d be remiss to exclude all of the the other standouts that helped Xander along the way: Josh Allen remaining the top QB in fantasy by about 30 points, 5th-round pick George Pickens ending up as the overall WR4 on the season and shattering all expectations, 10th-round pick Travis Etienne finishing as the RB9 on the season and being a very reliable and consistent second-scoring RB, and waiver wire pickup Jake Ferguson being the TE1 in the weeks where George Kittle was injured.

Truly, everything broke right for Xander. We asked for MORE, and boy did we get it. So congrats bud! Enjoy revelling in Austin’s misery as you watch him eat 10 wings so as to not pay you another penny. 

Although many of us playoff teams will wish to forget how this season ended, another year of Lakewood Legends is in the books. I appreciate all of your guys’ support on these silly little articles/blog posts/whatever you want to call this and for encouraging me to keep going with it. Can’t wait for the next Homies Fantasy Football trip, where for the ten year anniversary we hopefully do it up big. Cheers to hopefully an even better 2026 for everyone in the chat (including Photos, who I don’t think reads these) and I look forward to next fantasy season where we’ll probably see the Machine fail in some new way it has yet to fail and Austin will eat wings for the third year in a row! 🥂🍾

retrospective.intro:
Well gentlemen, we’ve finally made it. The new year is right around the corner, and our 17-week descent into madness is complete. Both congratulations and commiserations are due to the Smith brothers, who fulfilled their destinies as the regular season winner and loser to then become our postseason winner and loser as well. 

Now, with the power of hindsight, it’s only fair we look back at what I previously wrote about all of these teams throughout the year, and give you all the opportunity to dunk on me and let me know what I did and did not get right about you or your team. Join me in celebrating, commiserating, and humiliating the decisions that led us to where the 2025 fantasy season ended.

draft.label: Draft Recap

blurbs.1: While my love affair with Rocco’s team has come to its untimely end, I’m still finding reasons to lust after it. The big positive with Rocco’s team is that basically every pick is a talented player projected for high volume. The negative is that three of those top players represent the Titans, Jets, and Dolphins offenses, so maybe it’s perfectly accurate to call them all bums. Don’t be surprised when Rocco is averaging under 2 touchdowns a week after the first month.
blurbs.2: Richard usually ends up with sub-par drafts and finds his way into the playoffs anyway, so it’s likely this ranking will be complete hogwash like a month from now, but we rank rosters, not managers, and this roster is not incredibly inspiring. It should be stated that this felt low for Richard’s team, so I once again put it into a league analyzer and 113 fantasy “experts” also put his team 11th, so credit to me for checking my work. Also he called me the “weakest link” while we were getting rescued so, 🖕
blurbs.3: Matt forgot that Cam is the only one allowed to draft CMC and have it work out, the rest of us are doomed to fail when we take him. So, good luck with your 30-year-old high-volume running back with degenerative knees, alongside your two injury-prone New York Giants players. I’m sure that’ll work out spectacularly.
blurbs.4: Year after year, Tyler is getting slightly better at this whole drafting thing. Sure the team isn’t perfect, and he might have reached on his two RBs both rehabbing from season-ending injuries, and he took Bo Nix a bit too early. But honestly it’s not all that bad. Two elite WRs to start off, then Williams in the 5th, then you get some upside swings with Lloyd and Likely. There is very little separating this team from some of the top teams. It’s just that Ty is pretty used to being ranked down here, so why not do it again?
blurbs.5: It’s hard to rank a team with Jahmyr Gibbs any lower than 3rd, and Steve followed up pick 1 with a banger 2-3 turn. The picks get less and less good with each consecutive turn (some might say that’s how drafts usually work) but there’s a really strong foundation here. With some bounces the right way, and some good injury luck, it’d be easy to see this team as a championship contender. So, we know that’s not going to happen for Steven, and by picking Gibbs he’s doomed every other Gibbs owner. Probably.
blurbs.6: It’s gonna be difficult to criticize this team when the two best WRs in the NFL fell to him at crazy values in the first two rounds. I guess it’s not ideal to have a rookie RB in a committee as your RB2, and I guess I’d probably not have picked Johnson as TE1? Otherwise this is a solid team. Maybe it’s fitting that I give Nick 2nd place in these rankings, since he’s so used to finishing there. Always the bridesmaid.
blurbs.7: It’s possible this is me being humble and polite, not ranking myself first, and it’s possible I have beer goggles on and this team should be ranked far lower, but fuck it we ball. It’s hard for me to properly criticize my team, since I got basically exactly who I wanted when I wanted them, so I’ll try making the bear case for fun; I have two players on a bottom-12 projected offense, an injury-prone RB1 on a team who has consistently underperformed, the lowest-ranked starting QB of all of us, and a bunch of high-variance bums from rounds 5-7. So I guess it’s not all rosy over here (he says, lying).
blurbs.8: In what ended up an EXTREMELY tumultuous weekend for Cam, he started it out with a draft that was pretty nice. Securing two top-end RBs early, then filling the gaps with WRs and a top-tier fantasy QB is a pretty solid strategy. The big issue is that he took a WR with no toe, he fell into both the Marv trap AND the Pitts trap AGAIN, and he took a player who rehabbed his knee in jail. So sure, there’s reason to be optimistic, and maybe out of pity I should rank him higher, but 5 feels appropriate for a team with this many red flags.
blurbs.9: Every year, Connor pulls up to the draft not knowing a single player or rankings, reads an article like 30 minutes before draft time, drafts virtually only off of ESPN’s rankings and projected points, and ends up doing just fine. Considering how well the Quinshon pick worked out for him last year, it stands to reason that Josh Jacobs will probably end up being a good pick too. I mean, Connor took a team of shoestring and duct tape all the way to second place last year, maybe it’s my downfall that I should dare rank him this low.
blurbs.10: I can’t find a weakness in this team. If I squint, I could say taking a TE in the 5th and overlooking better flex depth is bad, or I could say that having limited WR depth would cripple this team. But those are really minor nitpicks; the foundation is extremely strong and picks 2-6 are all great value. Maybe this ranking is for drafting my favorite team, or maybe this is for lowkey saving my brother’s life on Sunday. In any case, Liam gets the post-draft crown. So congrats Liam, enjoy it while it lasts; you of all people should know that being number one in the power rankings means absolutely nothing!
blurbs.11: I watched my friends get swept away and stranded by a flash flood, stood in the pouring rain and freezing cold for three hours, and needed to get rescued with life jackets and ropes with the rest of us, yet seeing this team be assembled was the greatest disaster I witnessed this weekend. Bro doubled up on the Bears’ backfield and didn’t take his WR2 until round 8. Looks like my/our predictions that Austin will eat wings for the third year in a row already look pretty good.
blurbs.12: It seems that once again the Machine favors Xander over Austin, seeing as it gave him a far superior team. It’s possible the Machine employs some sort of positive reinforcement tactics and rewards Xander for his success while punishing Austin for his failures. While Xander does not know how to check the lock box outside of the house to find the keys, he DOES know how to check the waiver wire to find some gems — which is ultimately what led to his championship last year — so maybe we should expect similar success this season.

draft.intro: As we as a group get better and better at fantasy drafting, these rankings get harder and harder. Last year I said that it was definitely the hardest draft rankings I’ve had to do yet, but this year seemed harder. It would probably be far more appropriate to do a tier list, rather than ranking everyone individually, but that’s less fun and creates less engagement. I can’t wait until all of this is completely nullified after week 1, enjoy!

blurbs.1: In a normal week we could ask ourselves where we would have finished without Zay Flowers, but given that the opponent was Cam, who couldn’t even fart out 51 points, it’s best to just take the wins where we can get them. Sure, when we look in the rearview mirror, the danger of De’Von Achane playing like shit on a terrible offense is much closer than it appears, but let’s just ignore that for now.
blurbs.2: While I don’t appreciate the veiled threats, texted both in the group chat AND to me individually, AND calling me Fantasy Hitler, Richard’s team does have to see a rise in the ranks. It is ultimately discouraging to see so many high picks play so poorly, and without a Caleb Williams masterclass and Tyler benching his best-performing players this would’ve ended as an 0-2 week, we simply must be encouraged by the Bears’ offense and Jonny Blue Shoes playing well despite the Colts sucking. I’ll throw you down the ranks next week if you keep up the poor behavior though Rich. Remember the Golden Rule.
blurbs.3: Two good performances does not a team make. You just can’t have any confidence going forward in any of the low-end WRs and FLEX players on this team, and the team has already been bitten by the injury bug. It turns out investing in the Raiders, Giants, Cardinals, and Titans in the draft was a bad idea, who knew?
blurbs.4: Remember that year Tyler started like 10-0 and none of us knew what to do with ourselves? I was just thinking of that earlier. It’s nice that he’s fallen back into his usual niche, and I won’t have to freak out about his team anytime soon. I can’t be TOO harsh on Ty’s team; had he started his optimal lineup, he’d have won, so it’s more of a management issue than it is a personnel issue. Since he was the one who drafted it, maybe get Photos to manage your team for you too? Just a thought.
blurbs.5: Even in a week where Steven goes 2-0, his two RBs look great and combine for nearly 60 points, and his QB backdoors his way into a solid performance, he can’t escape the injury bug. It’s important to note that Steven’s 2nd-round pick, A.J. Brown, won’t be playing football for the next 4-6 weeks. This means that A.J. Brown, Steven’s 2nd-round pick, can’t be in Steven’s lineup. That’s just brutal. At least Gibbs is fun, and he’ll be totally fine handling all of this volume, right?
blurbs.6: An extreme rollercoaster of emotions saw Nick slam some things at his lowest and scream in elation at his highest, but in the end he managed to eke out a close one against Connor thanks to a last-second Justin Jefferson touchdown. Even with 1st-round pick Ja’Marr playing terribly, the team banded together and pulled through. I can’t wait for the inevitable 75-point performance and ensuing Nick crash out from this team next week.
blurbs.8: I mean, holy fuck. Not even one singular player in double digits this week. There’s just nothing to say. This is one of the league’s worst weekly performances ever. Where do you even go from here? Also, are you ready to admit I was right about Marv and Pitts? I await your apology.
blurbs.9: It turns out investing heavily into the Cooper Rush Falcons’ offense is a pretty good idea! Now, I’m confident Connor has no idea who Cooper Rush even is, nor did he watch a second of the games on Sunday, but he still motivated the boys to a 113-point performance so something is working in that locker room. We just need to see Connor channel his inner Coach Taylor for next week: clear eyes, full hearts, can’t lose.
blurbs.10: This is where we get the big boys, the four 2-0 teams with perfect starts. It was tough to find ranks for everyone, so since Liam specifically asked to be lower than rank 1 last week, I figured I’d give it to him. That, plus he invested heavily into the Chargers, who fucking sucked on Sunday, leads him to be 4th. But hey, maybe now that Liam’s not first and my jinx on him is gone, we’ll see James Cook and George Pickens actually do something next week. That must’ve been why they sucked.
blurbs.11: It’s always tough when you come up against an unstoppable buzzsaw, but credit where credit’s due, the Machine held up well. I can’t rank it TOO high, considering its best wide receiver performance was Jalen Nailor’s 4.2 points, and I still don’t feel particularly optimistic about a) this team’s long-term outlook and b) Austin’s ability to navigate the waiver wire. But, this is likely one of the few wins the Machine will get this year, so it’s only fair we let Austin celebrate it.
blurbs.12: Just a brutal Monday night performance from Dobbins takes Xander from a 2-0 team to an 0-2 team. Some unfortunate underperformances here in this lineup, but with just how hot the running backs ran, and how good the receivers should be the rest of the year, and how close this team came to a perfect start, I can’t move this team down. Not just yet. I have faith in the young Machine.
